rules.title: Annual rent increase limit and frequency
rules.requirement: Covered rent increases may not exceed the lesser of 3% or 80% of the specified Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim CPI change, and only one increase is permitted in any twelve-month period; a negative CPI change permits no increase. Serving a notice or demand for a prohibited increase constitutes a violation.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI; one increase per 12 months; no increase if CPI is negative
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to Owners/Landlords offering residential real property or mobilehome spaces for rent in Santa Ana, including lessors, sublessors, successors and employees or representatives with authority to bind the landlord. Rent includes periodic monetary and nonmonetary compensation and associated housing services; reducing housing services without a corresponding rent reduction is a rent increase. Excludes residential property with a certificate of occupancy issued after February 1, 1995 and other applicable Costa-Hawkins exemptions; mobilehome spaces under qualifying agreements longer than one year, newly constructed spaces first offered for rent on or after January 1, 1990, mobilehomes not used as a person's primary residence and not leased to someone else, and other applicable Mobilehome Residency Law exemptions. Section 8-3147 also excludes specified deed-restricted or government-agreement affordable or subsidized housing for very-low-, low- or moderate-income households; dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or K–12 school; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; and two dwellings in one structure where the owner has continuously occupied one as a principal residence since tenancy inception and neither is an ADU or junior ADU. Separately alienable housing is exempt only if the owner is neither a REIT, corporation nor LLC with a corporate member and tenants receive the prescribed exemption notice, which must be in the rental agreement for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after ordinance effectiveness. Approved fair-return relief is available under sections 8-3141–8-3145; capital-improvement and registry-fee pass-throughs have separate restrictions and are excluded from rent as specified. Statutory cross-references and the annual exemption-claim requirements of section 8-3160(d) require execution review.

rules.requirement: The City must announce the allowable rent increase by June 30 each year, with that annual amount effective September 1.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to the City of Santa Ana in its role calculating and announcing the annual permissible increase under section 8-3140(a); it does not impose an increase or establish that any particular rental property is covered.

rules.title: Capital-improvement pass-through restrictions
rules.requirement: A capital-improvement pass-through must be amortized over the improvement's useful life, may not exceed 10% of current rent excluding such pass-throughs, must deduct reimbursements, use only residential square footage for mixed-use structures and landlord-occupied units, and include agent-occupied units in average costs. Pass-throughs are not rent, cannot increase with rent, and cannot be included when calculating a rent increase.
rules.key_value: At most 10% of current rent, amortized over useful life
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a Landlord, including a lessor, sublessor, successor or representative authorized to bind the landlord, obtaining a capital-improvement pass-through through the Division 3 petition process for a nonexempt Santa Ana Rental Unit. The improvement must have been paid for and completed after November 19, 2021 and before filing; the petition must be initiated within two years of completion. A qualifying improvement has a useful life of at least five years and requires amortization; routine maintenance, repair, replacement and deterioration from unreasonable delay or after an agency repair notice do not qualify. The improvement must primarily benefit tenants, be permanently fixed or relatively immobile, and carry no use fee. Units or new tenants whose initial rent was established after completion are excluded; tenants cannot be charged for periods without entitlement to occupancy, more than their unit's permitted share, or improvements benefiting only other units. Relevant Division 3 exemptions include post-February 1, 1995 certificates and other Costa-Hawkins exemptions; qualifying mobilehome agreements longer than one year, new spaces first offered on or after January 1, 1990, non-primary-residence mobilehomes not leased to others, and other Mobilehome Residency Law exemptions; specified restricted/subsidized affordable housing; school-owned-and-operated dormitories; certificates issued within the previous 15 years; continuously owner-occupied two-unit structures from tenancy inception with neither unit an ADU or junior ADU; and separately alienable dwellings with a non-REIT, noncorporate owner and no corporate LLC member, plus the prescribed notice, placed in the agreement for post-effective-date commencements or renewals. No landlord petition or upward adjustment is authorized following continued noncompliance after a Board order or failure to satisfy habitability requirements. Statutory exemptions, annual exemption claims and the provision's stated July 1, 2023 start subject to Council modification require review.

rules.title: Tenant petitions and filing deadlines
rules.requirement: A covered tenant may petition to review an excessive increase, reduce rent for decreased services or uninhabitability, contest an unauthorized or excessive capital-improvement pass-through, or address another Article violation. Applicable filing limits are 30 days after service of an increase notice, 30 days after learning of noncompliance when required notice was omitted, and 180 days after other alleged violations.

rules.title: Noncompliance bars landlord petitions and upward adjustments
rules.requirement: No landlord petition or upward rent adjustment under Division 3 is authorized if the landlord continues noncompliance after a Board order or has failed to bring the unit into compliance with the implied warranty of habitability.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a Landlord seeking a petition or upward adjustment under Santa Ana Division 3 for a Rental Unit subject to that Division, where either stated noncompliance condition exists. Landlord includes owners, lessors, sublessors, successors and representatives with authority to bind the landlord. Rent-regulation exemptions encompass post-February 1, 1995 certificates and other Costa-Hawkins exemptions; qualifying mobilehome leases longer than one year, new spaces first offered on or after January 1, 1990, non-primary-residence mobilehomes not leased to others, and other Mobilehome Residency Law exemptions; specified restricted/subsidized affordable housing; school-owned-and-operated dormitories; certificates issued within the previous 15 years; qualifying continuously owner-occupied two-unit structures from tenancy inception without ADUs or junior ADUs; and separately alienable housing with an owner that is neither a REIT, corporation nor LLC with a corporate member and the prescribed tenant notice, in the agreement for post-effective-date commencements or renewals. Annual exemption claims and incorporated statutory exemptions require execution review.

rules.title: Rental Registry Fee pass-through limit
rules.requirement: After timely payment, a landlord may pass through at most 50% of the Registry Fee in twelve equal monthly installments, excluding it from rent-increase calculations; delinquent fees and penalties cannot be passed through. No portion may be charged to the specified affordable or subsidized tenants, and excess pass-through payments must be reimbursed.

rules.title: Registration prerequisite to advertising and collecting rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not advertise a covered unit for rent or demand or accept its rent without complete and accurate registration. Petitions, applications, claims, requests and rent increases cannot take effect without accurately completed registration.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a Landlord with a Santa Ana Rental Unit subject to Article XIX and its Rental Registry requirements, including owners, lessors, sublessors, successors and representatives authorized to bind the landlord. Complete registration requires all City fees and penalties to be paid and a complete, accurate form containing the information required by Division 4 and implementing policies. Registration duties include initial and annual registration, changes of ownership or management, re-registration after vacancy and re-rental, and registration after loss of exemption; annual exemption declarations and supporting documents are required under section 8-3160(d). Rent and termination exemptions are provision-specific, so neither alone establishes exemption from the entire Article or Registry. The stated October 1, 2023 enforcement commencement and the Article's later voter-approval effectiveness require review.

rules.title: Just cause after thirty days of lawful occupancy
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied covered residential real property for 30 days, the owner may terminate only for just cause stated in a written termination notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to an Owner offering Santa Ana residential real property for rent, including lessors, sublessors, successors and representatives authorized to bind the landlord, after the tenant's continuous lawful occupancy for 30 days. Termination provisions exclude mobilehomes and mobilehome spaces subject to Civil Code section 798.56. Section 8-3120(e) excludes transient/tourist hotel occupancy; accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended-care facilities, licensed elderly residential-care facilities or specified adult residential facilities; dormitories owned and operated by higher-education institutions or K–12 schools; shared kitchen/bath housing where the owner maintains a principal residence; owner-occupied single-family residences, including those renting no more than two units or bedrooms, including ADUs or junior ADUs; duplexes continuously occupied by the owner as a principal residence since tenancy inception; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the preceding 15 years; and specified deed-restricted or government-agreement affordable/subsidized housing for very-low-, low- or moderate-income households. Separately alienable dwellings are exempt only when the owner is neither a REIT, corporation nor LLC with a corporate member and tenants receive the prescribed notice, included in the rental agreement for tenancies commenced or renewed after ordinance effectiveness, with agreement placement optional for earlier tenancies. Just cause is governed by the specified at-fault and no-fault grounds and their qualifications in section 8-3120(b). Annual exemption-claim requirements and incorporated statutory definitions require execution review.

rules.title: Protection for qualifying replacement subleases
rules.requirement: An owner cannot terminate for a qualifying one-for-one replacement sublease when the tenant requests permission in writing, remains in the property as a primary residence and receives no written response within a reasonable time. For leases of one year or less, the unanswered request is deemed approved.

A reasonable refusal may include occupancy exceeding Uniform Housing Code section 503(b) or its successor. Owner includes lessors, sublessors, successors and representatives authorized to bind the landlord. Excludes Civil Code section 798.56 mobilehome terminations; transient/tourist hotels; specified nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care, licensed elderly residential-care and adult residential facilities; school-owned-and-operated dormitories; owner-principal-residence shared kitchen/bath housing; owner-occupied single-family residences including up to two rented units/bedrooms; duplexes continuously owner-occupied principally from tenancy inception; certificates issued within 15 years; specified restricted/subsidized affordable housing; and separately alienable dwellings with a non-REIT, noncorporate owner and no corporate LLC member plus prescribed notice, in the agreement for post-effective-date commencements or renewals. rules.title: Demolition or substantial-remodel return protections
rules.requirement: For the demolition-or-substantial-remodel ground, the owner must give advance notice of reoccupancy after repairs or, at the tenant's request, first refusal of an owner-held comparable vacant unit offered at comparable rent. If the owner seeks to rent the remodeled unit within six months after work is completed, the evicted tenant has first refusal to return unless the owner provides the tenant's written waiver.

Owner includes lessors, sublessors, successors and authorized representatives. rules.title: No-fault relocation payment or rent waiver
rules.requirement: For a covered no-fault termination, regardless of income, the owner must notify the tenant of applicable rights and either pay three months of rent within 15 calendar days after notice service or waive the final three months in writing before rent is due, using the rent in effect when notice was issued and stating the waiver amount and that no final-three-month rent is due. rules.title: Documented abuse-victim defense to possession
rules.requirement: A tenant has a defense when the trier of fact finds that the tenant or household member has qualifying abuse documentation from the preceding 180 days and the notice substantially rests on that abuse. The stated exceptions permit termination when the protected person allows the identified perpetrator to visit, or when the owner reasonably believes that person's presence poses the specified threat and previously gave a three-day cease-and-correct notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to an Owner's Division 2 possession action concerning a covered Santa Ana Rental Unit and a tenant or household member subjected to domestic violence, elder or dependent-adult abuse, sexual assault, human trafficking or stalking. Documentation must be a qualifying protective or restraining order issued within 180 days or a police report filed within 180 days; the notice must be substantially based on the abusive acts, including related noise, disturbances or repeated police presence. The tenant must fall within section 8-3120's 30-day continuous lawful occupancy protection; Owner includes lessors, sublessors, successors and authorized representatives. Excludes Civil Code section 798.56 mobilehome terminations; transient/tourist hotels; specified nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care, licensed elderly residential-care and adult residential facilities; school-owned-and-operated dormitories; owner-principal-residence shared kitchen/bath housing; owner-occupied single-family residences including up to two rented units/bedrooms; duplexes continuously owner-occupied principally since tenancy inception; certificates within 15 years; specified restricted/subsidized affordable housing; and separately alienable dwellings with a non-REIT, noncorporate owner and no corporate LLC member plus prescribed notice, in agreements commenced or renewed after effectiveness. The reasonable-threat exception concerns other tenants, guests, invitees or a tenant's quiet enjoyment and requires the prior three-day notice. Other referenced victim-protection laws and annual exemption claims require review.

rules.title: Retaliatory termination and nonrenewal prohibited
rules.requirement: If retaliation is the owner's main intent and the tenant is not in rent default, the owner may not terminate, refuse renewal or cause involuntary departure; retaliation for exercising Article rights is also prohibited. Tenants may assert retaliation affirmatively or defensively regardless of elapsed time, but retaliation claims must be brought in court rather than administratively.

Tenant and Tenancy use the Article's Rental Unit definition, which excludes units exempt under applicable Article provisions. Section 8-3120(e) exemptions are expressly limited to that section, so neither those exemptions nor the 30-day just-cause threshold is treated as an established exemption from section 8-3122; provision-specific Article coverage and annual exemption claims require execution review.

“Rent” means all periodic compensation, including all non-monetary
consideration, that a Tenant provides to a Landlord concerning the use or
occupancy of a Rental Unit, including any amount included in the Rent for
utilities (unless separately billed to the Tenant by the utility company),
parking, storage, pets or for any other fee or charge associated with the
Tenancy for the use or occupancy of a Rental Unit and related Housing
Services.

Increases in Rent on Residential Real Property or Mobilehome Spaces in
             the City of Santa Ana in excess of three percent (3%), or eighty (80%) of
             the change in the Consumer Price Index, whichever is less, and more than
             one Rent Increase in any twelve (12) month period, are prohibited, unless
             expressly exempt under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act codified in
             California Civil Code section 1954.50, et seq., or the Mobilehome
             Residency Law codified in California Civil Code sections 798, et seq.
